architectureFigure.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the unified supervision framework for large-scale e-commerce retrieval. The system integrates human and relevance cross encoder labeled relevance scores, item ranks from existing retrieval channels, and user engagement signals to generate a context-rich supervision target to train bi-encoder model.

authors: Shasvat Desai, Md Omar Faruk Rokon, Jhalak Nilesh Acharya, Isha Shah, Hong Yao, Utkarsh Porwal, Kuang-chih Lee

breakthroughAssessment.justification: The paper provides a robust industrial solution for the common problem of sparse and noisy engagement data in sponsored search by synthesizing LLM-distilled relevance labels with production rank priors and engagement signals into a unified training target.

coreProblem.concreteExample: In Walmart's sponsored search, a highly relevant ad for organic milk might not receive clicks (engagement) simply because the advertiser's budget ran out or it lost the auction for a prominent slot, leading a model trained only on engagement to incorrectly learn that the ad is irrelevant.
coreProblem.statement: Standard engagement-based supervision for retrieval is noisy and structurally sparse in sponsored search due to ad-slot auctions, budgets, and limited display positions.
whyItMatters: Biases models towards popular but weakly relevant items
Limits the learnability of cold-start and long-tail items
Engagement signals do not perfectly align with semantic relevance

evaluationHighlights: Offline evaluation on 30,303 queries covering head and long-tail traffic
Online A/B testing on live Walmart production traffic
Ablation study comparing relevance-only vs. relevance-plus-engagement supervision

evaluationSetup.setting: Retrieval of top-25 items from the full catalog indexed using FAISS

keyResults.metric: Total Search Page Views per Session

keyResultGroups.title: A/B Test Results: Business and Engagement Metrics

mainTakeaways: Semantic relevance should define retrieval eligibility, while engagement should refine preference among relevant items.
Unified supervision significantly outperforms production systems using only engagement signals.
Incorporating production rank priors helps the model identify and learn from hard negatives.

explanation: Uses a multi-stage LLM cascade (Gemma-1B, Gemma-2B, Llama-3 8B) for efficient high-quality relevance labeling.
Synthesizes three heterogeneous signals (graded relevance, retrieval priors, and engagement) into a single continuous training target.
Formulates an Irrelevant QIP Difficulty Score to prioritize hard negatives based on retrieval rank and lexical overlap.
keyNovelty.main: A unified supervision framework that makes semantic relevance the primary signal for bi-encoder training while using engagement only to refine ordering among relevant candidates.

keyTerms.definition: A retrieval architecture that independently encodes queries and items into a vector space for fast similarity search.
Historical user interactions such as clicks, views, and add-to-carts.
The process of selecting difficult negative examples (items not relevant to the query but highly ranked) to improve model discriminative power.

prerequisites: Basic understanding of neural information retrieval
Familiarity with cross-encoder and bi-encoder architectures
Knowledge of e-commerce search ranking metrics like NDCG and Precision

comparisonToPriorWork: Prior methods usually treat engagement as the primary signal and use relevance for filtering; this work reverses the hierarchy.
Integrates production rank priors as a signal for hard negative mining, which is rarely done in standard distillation frameworks.
limitations: Reliance on LLM-based labeling might introduce teacher biases into the bi-encoder.
The framework is optimized for sponsored search and may require tuning for organic search.

modeling.label: Loss Function
modeling.value: Cosine Similarity Loss and Cached Multiple Negatives Ranking (MNR) Loss

pipelineFlow: 1. Candidate Generation: Sample Query-Item Pairs (QIPs) from various traffic segments.
2. Relevance Labeling: Apply a cascaded LLM (Gemma/Llama) teacher model to generate graded relevance scores.
3. Prior Computation: Extract rank positions and channel consensus from production retrieval logs.
4. Engagement Aggregation: Compute log-compressed, weighted interaction counts for QIPs.
5. Unified Scoring: Combine relevance, prior, and engagement into a single target score using a weighted fusion.
6. Model Training: Fine-tune MiniLM bi-encoder via contrastive learning and curriculum-based negative sampling.

problemDefinition.label: Target
problemDefinition.value: Minimize retrieval errors in sponsored search by defining a training objective that is robust to sparse engagement data.

problemDefinition.label: Unified Score
problemDefinition.value: $y_{rel-rank}(q, i) = \alpha \cdot rel\_score(q, i) + \beta \cdot \pi(q, i) + \gamma \cdot C(q, i)$

technicalDetails.reproducibility: The methodology is described in detail, including specific LLM models used (Gemma, Llama-3) and hyperparameter values for weights (alpha, beta, gamma). Internal Walmart data prevents direct replication.

systemModules.details: Annotates QIPs on a 5-point scale using a cascade of Gemma-1B, Gemma-2B, and Llama-3 8B.
systemModules.name: Relevance Cascade
systemModules.role: Provides the primary semantic supervision signal.

systemModules.details: Maps rank positions from multiple production channels into a normalized monotonic prior.
systemModules.name: Multi-channel Prior
systemModules.role: Identifies established system strengths and facilitates hard negative mining.

systemModules.details: Aggregates orders, clicks, and views into a weighted, log-compressed score.
systemModules.name: Engagement Module
systemModules.role: Refines ordering among semantically relevant candidates.

thesis: In sponsored search, bi-encoder retrievers should be trained with semantic relevance as the foundation of the objective, using behavioral engagement only to refine preferences among relevant candidates to overcome data sparsity and noise.
title: Unified Supervision for Walmart’s Sponsored Search Retrieval via Joint Semantic Relevance and Behavioral Engagement Modeling
